issue_context.title: NetworkPolicySpec field doc is outdated
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I tried to understand exactly what NetworkPolicy objects mean, and got lost/confused.  https://groups.google.com/g/kubernetes-sig-network/c/6k1A8l5uxLY

For example, the comments on the `PolicyTypes` field does not precisely specify semantics, and the comments on the `Ingress` and `Egress` fields omit the significance of the `PolicyTypes` field.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected to find clear answers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Try to figure out from the comments in `types.go` exactly how the `PolicyType` field of a `NetworkPolicySpec` interacts with the `Ingress` and `Egress` fields.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

review_comments: The standard way of describing NetworkPolicy is that pods are either isolated or not isolated, and NetworkPolicy only applies to isolated pods. Pods become isolated for ingress by having an ingress NetworkPolicy select them, and pods become isolated for egress by having an egress NetworkPolicy select them.
As you say, there are two directions of isolation.  A pod is _not_ simply "isolated" or not.

Also, I think that in plain English, "isolated" is an absolute thing (no exceptions) whereas "restricted" is not absolute (there are some exceptions).  What we mean here is not an absolute but rather a matter of imposing some limits.
If all of this belongs anywhere in the API documentation it seems like it belongs at the top level in the documentation of `NetworkPolicy` as a whole, not in the documentation of `PodSelector`
The comment on the NetworkPolicy type does not get into the generated API page, right?

"initiation" is not a standard term and it's not obvious here that you're using it to mean both the sending side and the receiving side of the connection establishment process, as opposed to just the sending side.

The phrasing that people normally use is that NetworkPolicy applies to connections, not to packets
Do you think that if I simply say "connection" that the reader will understand that this applies to UDP as well?
NetworkPolicy can not talk about egress from an IP block, right?

A NetworkPolicy necessarily applies to a pod, right?  It is in the characterization of the peer that IP blocks are used.  The existing language covers the case of a connection between a pod and a non-pod.
